stem: When counseling a candidate about pancreas transplant alone (PTA) eligibility, which metabolic criterion aligns with standard references?

options.text: On insulin with C-peptide ≤ 2 ng/mL, or on insulin with C-peptide ≥ 2 ng/mL and BMI ≤ 28 kg/m²
No insulin use and elevated C-peptide as the sole requirement
BMI greater than 35 kg/m² as a required inclusion criterion for every PTA candidate
PTA is indicated only when the candidate no longer has diabetes

explanation.rationale_correct: PTA candidates must meet insulin and C-peptide criteria such as on insulin with C-peptide ≤ 2 ng/mL, or on insulin with C-peptide ≥ 2 ng/mL and BMI at or below the maximum allowable BMI (currently ≤ 28 kg/m²).

rationale_incorrect.B: PTA candidates are insulin-treated with specified C-peptide and BMI thresholds rather than insulin-free status.
rationale_incorrect.C: A maximum allowable BMI threshold applies rather than requiring obesity.
rationale_incorrect.D: PTA is for candidates with diabetes meeting metabolic criteria, not for resolved diabetes.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: On insulin and C-peptide ≤ 2 ng/mL OR On insulin and C-peptide ≥2 ng/mL AND … BMI … ≤28 kg/m2

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 15 → Indications → A.1.b. (PTA insulin/C-peptide and BMI criteria); PDF p. 825 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. PTA metabolic-criteria angle distinct from hypoglycemic-unawareness counseling (cctc-1062) and SPK indication (cctc-2067); anchor verified on Cupples p. 825.

stem: A coordinator is updating parvovirus B19 teaching for transplant families. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Parvovirus B19 is typically acquired during the school-age period.
Parvovirus may cause pure red blood cell aplasia with low hematocrit.
Parvovirus infection occurs only in adult transplant recipients.
A slapped-cheek rash may be part of the clinical presentation.

explanation.rationale_correct: Parvovirus B19 is typically acquired during school age, may cause pure red blood cell aplasia with low hematocrit, and may present with a slapped-cheek rash. It is not limited to adult recipients, so statement III is false.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—slapped-cheek rash may occur.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false—parvovirus is classically acquired in school-age children.

stem: When educating a liver transplant candidate about hepatorenal complications of advanced liver disease, which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Hepatorenal failure may involve rapid renal-function decline and require dialysis
Hepatorenal failure never requires renal replacement therapy
Hepatorenal failure is treated primarily with isolated kidney transplantation without liver transplant
Renal dysfunction never occurs in advanced liver disease

explanation.rationale_correct: Hepatorenal failure involves a rapid decrease in renal function in patients with advanced liver disease and may need to be treated with dialysis.

rationale_incorrect.B: Dialysis may be required when hepatorenal failure develops.
rationale_incorrect.C: In the setting of advanced liver disease, hepatorenal syndrome is addressed through liver transplantation rather than isolated kidney transplant alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Hepatorenal failure is a recognized complication of advanced liver disease.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 12, Liver Transplantation → Hepatic encephalopathy / hepatorenal → 6.

stem: During living donor informed consent, which confirmation must the donor provide in writing per standard references?

options.text: That he or she is willing to donate
That the recipient surgeon has unlimited authority to override donor withdrawal
That the donor will never need any post-donation follow-up
That financial compensation for donation is expected

explanation.rationale_correct: The donor must confirm in writing that he or she is willing to donate, is free from inducement and coercion, may decline at any time, and understands federal prohibitions on organ sales.

rationale_incorrect.B: Donors retain the right to decline donation; surgeons do not override that autonomy.
rationale_incorrect.C: Donors commit to postoperative follow-up coordinated by the live donor program.
rationale_incorrect.D: Federal law prohibits offering organs for anything of value rather than expecting compensation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Care of Living Donors → F. Elements Included in Education and Informed Consent → 1.a.
